articleTitle: Designing A Secure Smart Healthcare System with Blockchain: A Review
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) is the new development of Information Technology which connects the devices with Internet to make them smart. IoT has a variety of applications viz., smart healthcare, smart transport, smart agriculture, and smart city. Healthcare IoT facilitates correspondence between doctors and patients. The patients can be analysed remotely in critical situations with help of smart wearable devices. Healthcare records are very sensitive and any violation can cause unwanted severe consequences. Therefore, patients' data must be highly secured. Blockchain helps to maintain the high-level security in the healthcare IoT. Blockchain also provides immutability and confidentiality. This paper presents a brief survey on security in healthcare IoT with blockchain. We found that security can be enhanced in healthcare framework using blockchain.

articleTitle: Reimagining the Future of Communication with 5G Networks
abstract: Wireless communication technologies have evolved tremendously over the years and they are continuing to do so. Developed with a vision to provide unrivaled data rates and uninterrupted connectivity in all parts of the world, 5G will be a driving force in an attempt to bring a massive revolution in the existing landscape of information and communication technology (ICT) industry. In my view, 4G was a promising new technology, but 5G is the ultimate deal-breaker, with features and capabilities that have the potential to bring a significant change in the arena of wireless communications. 5G doesn't undermine the outstanding impact that the legacy core (LTE) networks have had. Moreover, while introducing new features like IoT and cloud computing, 5G is also focused on eradicating the limitations that 4G networks had to a great extent. This paper focuses on discussing in detail the characteristics and components of 5G networks that justify the anticipation that it has been creating over the years and concludes with discussing the impact of the recent pandemic on 5G.

articleTitle: Prediction of Customer Retention Rate Employing Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: In the recent decade, telecom sector is subjected to major revolution in the terms of subscribers' count and the technological content. Owing to institutional and policy reforms that have liberalized the sector, there is a significant rise in competition among telecom companies. With companies experiencing an ever-increasing rate of customer churn rate, and as it is costlier to acquire a new customer than to retain an existing one, customer retention has become one of the prime focus of companies. Enterprises and managers are focusing on improving customer retention rate now more than ever. With the large amount of customer data at our disposal, machine learning algorithms are apt for the efficient analysis of such data. This study compares the accuracy of traditional data mining techniques viz Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree, XGBoost, Random Forest, Light Gradient Boosting, Gradient Descent Boosting and Cat Boost in predicting customer churn and then proposes an algorithm based on the above techniques that aims to find the major causes for customer churn from one company to another and the ways in which enterprises can improve customer retention. The reduced set of relevant features are selected by employing our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of COVID-19 Tweets
abstract: Sentiment analysis is the field of computer science that studies people's behaviour or attitude towards objects, events, organizations, and products. Organizations make use of this to improve their products. This paper aims to study people's behaviour towards COVID 19. We have taken data from Twitter to analyse the sentiments. The results show that people don't have positive sentiments towards this coronavirus.

articleTitle: Internet of Everything: Application and Various Challenges Analysis a Survey
abstract: The Internet of Everything (IoE) is a fast-growing field with capabilities to revolutionize the whole industry. As per market trends, more than 20 billion smart devices will be deployed in the next 5 years. These interconnected devices will be generating sensitive data which needs to be protected. The field of IoE is making leaps and bounds technologically. In this survey we throw light on new domains that can benefit from IoE, along with presenting a comprehensive study of available hardware, software, infrastructure, communication protocols, attack classification, attack surfaces and individual layer security.

articleTitle: Hand-Written Characters Recognition using Siamese Network Design
abstract: Hand-written documents are being digitalized and various traditional approaches have been merged to automatically recognize the syntax and semantic of target statement. However, real time applications such as bank data processing and security are still challenging due to the variation in human hand-written document. Similarly, traditional assistive scheme requires large amount of data to learn new features and their pattern. To deal with this, one-shot learning scheme is employed to recognize hand-written characters using Siamese network architecture. The Siamese network can compute the similarity or difference between two data samples and also effective to process unseen data that has not been previously trained. Additionally, convolutional neural network architecture is fused up to extract significant features during training and provides the stability in learning. The performance is validated through standard evaluation measures operated on the public dataset.

articleTitle: Big Data in Healthcare: A Review
abstract: Big data is affecting practically every part of our lives whether it's for political campaigns, retail purchases, surveying telescopic information, or recommendation algorithms. The goal of this study is to give a broad review of recent breakthroughs in big data in biomedical and health informatics. Recent developments in big data are projected to expand our knowledge by revealing illness causes and consequences, identifying better drug targets for precision medicine, and testing novel theories regarding disease prevention from diagnosis to inhibition to tailored treatment. This paper examines the main aspects of big data, some of the current and prospective opportunities in the field of big data for healthcare.

articleTitle: Simulation Model For Wireless Body Area Network Using Castalia
abstract: Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) is an emerging field in healthcare sector which facilitates remote monitoring by gathering health related data using wearable bio-sensors based on IOT. This technological advancement would significantly improve the tracking of fitness, healthcare delivery, medical diagnostics, early disease prediction and associated medical dealings of any individual. Castalia 3.2 is OMNET++ based simulator for wireless sensor network (WSN), patient monitoring or body area network (BAN) and other low power networks. Its scalable model offers a flexible framework that allows testing new algorithms and protocols for specific applications. The proposed model comprised of five sensor nodes along with a coordinator node. Sensor nodes include electrocardiography (ECG), Blood Oxygen Saturation (SpO2), Blood Pressure, Body Temperature and Body motion. A number of protocols are being proposed on the different layers of WBAN. This paper provides guidance for simulation of various scenarios and characteristics of Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs) and also furnishes an assessment of quality metrics using Castalia 3.2 Simulator with OMNET++ framework.

articleTitle: A Frog based Nature Inspired Algorithm for Solving Optimization Problem
abstract: Humans have always been inspired by nature, and they have continued to adapt and absorb various environmental systems. Several Nature Inspired Algorithms have been created and used to a wide range of challenging engineering optimization problems. The self-defense strategy used by prey animals prompted us to write this paper. In nature, we see that one species is the food of another, implying that one animal's survival is dependent on the survival of another. As a result, individuals are exposed to a variety of dangers in their daily lives. As a result, many species develop defense mechanisms to avoid becoming prey to another predator animal. The suggested Improved Anti-predatory Nature Inspired algorithm (IAPNIA) is inspired by frogs' self-defense strategies for survival. We have improved the directional flee functionality of the algorithm by observing that the frog can only observe the nearest peer frog and thus makes a jump towards it. The suggested method's findings were compared to the existing Anti-predatory Nature Inspired Algorithm (APNIA). We tested the algorithm on 10 benchmark functions and compared it with the existing APNIA, in which we performed better in 5 benchmarks and similar in 4 benchmarks. We also compared the convergence plots on 6 benchmark functions on which our algorithm converges faster than the existing APNIA. This demonstrates the value of the proposed algorithm in terms of convergence and quality of the solution achieved.

articleTitle: Intelligent Intrusion Detection System Optimized using Nature-Inspired Algorithms
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems are the software or applications which are positioned on network and host terminals to monitor the data that passes through those points. There are numerous kinds of Intrusion Detection Systems which either detect malicious behaviour of unauthorized user by matching his signature with already collected ones or by classifying it into normal or malicious access. The aim of this paper is to propose an Intrusion Detection System which is not domain specific, generic in nature and can be used both for detection of intrusions in a network or a computer. The algorithms proposed in this paper are optimized using nature inspired algorithms and based on Supervised and Unsupervised Learning Models. The usage of Nature Inspired Optimization Algorithms reduced the computational overhead of the proposed algorithms significantly. The proposed algorithms were validated and tested on three leading datasets from Network Security field namely, KDD99, ADFA and UNSW. The quality results generated on these datasets validate the use of these algorithms for Intrusion Detection in the real world.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach for Obstacle Classification in Automotive Radar
abstract: Machine Learning and Deep Learning have made a significant contribution in camera sensor perception, but not much to the Radar sensor, because of its time-series nature of the data and system complexity. Radar is mostly used for object detection and tracking, perception using Radar is not explored as camera sensor. Our previous work on the moving object classification [6] is another attempt for introducing machine learning in Radar systems. In this paper, we discuss the different machine learning/deep learning architecture-based obstacle classification in Radar data for automotive application. We propose novel architectures that can handle time series and instantaneous data simultaneously for classification. Neural Network, LSTM, 1D-CNN, and hybrid architecture are explored in this paper.

articleTitle: B-LIAR: A novel model for handling Multiclass Fake News data utilizing a Transformer Encoder Stack-based architecture
abstract: In today's digital era, social media is involved in purposely pushing fake news over the web to increase the readership of the people. Various techniques that are adopted for propagation are clickbait that works by posting content that attracts the users with flashy headlines to increase their advertisement reviews. Other methodologies include satire content which publishes fake news mainly for entertainment, sloppy journalism where sometimes reporters or journalists publish stories without complete reliable information which leads to misinformation to the audience. Therefore, a detection system is necessary as it can help national security agencies, investigation departments, businesses, the industry in detecting fake news in social media. In this paper, for the detection of fake news, we have used the LIAR dataset. This dataset consists of 12.8k manually labelled sentences from PolitiFact.com in various contexts. We have deployed a novel attention approach for detection using BERT embedding in our proposed model. Using our proposed model, we have reached the state-of-the-art result compared to the existing methods. The results obtained from our experiments showcase that our model can be used by researchers for further exploration.

articleTitle: Analytical Prediction and Sentimental Analysis of virtual engagement tools in teens and youth of urban and rural areas in India
abstract: Chatting, educational project discussions, and attending live events via different digital platforms are among the ways that today's youth use technology. Although the utilization of virtual engagement tools by youngsters has been studied in other countries, less is known about the online behaviors of Indian teens and youth in both urban and rural India. So, I have carried out an analysis on the factors “Age, Gender, Area they live (Rural or Urban), familiarity and user satisfaction for educational project discussions platforms, instant messaging and informal chatting platforms, and platforms for attending live virtual events”. Based on these parameters, I created 3 prediction models which utilize supervised learning and involve Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Linear Kernel SVM, and Polynomial Kernel SVM. Considering the data collected, it predicts “which platform to utilize taking into account the rural and urban India”. In all these three models, the highest accuracies were obtained by the Random Forest algorithm. The highest accuracy obtained by the model which predicts a platform for educational project discussions is ~79%. The highest accuracy obtained by the model which predicts a platform for informal chatting is ~90%. The highest accuracy obtained by the model which predicts a platform for attending live virtual events is ~85%. Sentimental Analysis of these platforms is performed based on the reviews of the respondents. This highlights and helps to gauge how to improve the user experience.

articleTitle: Tunnel Detection for Automotive Radar using Object Elevation Trends and Gaussian Filtering
abstract: This paper presents detection of tunnels based on object elevation property and gaussian filtering. Tunnel detection is essential to avoid false events in Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) and Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) functionalities. The new feature presented in this paper is one of the methods for tunnel detection. This method concentrates on the elevation history of objects in a specified region of interest. The feature helps to detect less reflective tunnels, curvy tunnels, tunnels with varying patterns of ceiling lights and some short tunnels. The use of gaussian filtering is done to filter out elevated objects from side guardrails and trees to avoid any false tunnel activation. The fusion of this new feature with the existing algorithm helps in improving the tunnel true positive rate by ~3.5% and reducing the tunnel false positive rate by ~4%.

articleTitle: Automatic Stance Detection for Twitter Data
abstract: Stance detection is a measure to understand the user view over the content posted on social media. Research associated with stance detection also includes modeling text to identify trends, opinions, feedback, reviews, and political alignment of users on social media. This paper focuses on identifying user stance for the 2019 Indian General election. We collected the data with a hashtag search. We have applied machine learning classifier and neural network approaches to detect user stance.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition Using Deep Learning
abstract: It is widely accepted that poor hygiene and irresponsible behavior of humans towards their health are major reasons for diseases in developing countries. The maintenance of cleanliness at public places is very much required for everyone. This paper focuses to automate the process to detect un-hygienic activities anywhere, especially at public places, organizations such as offices, schools, colleges, etc., and to detect and recognize the persons. It can further be used to arrange hygiene sanitation workshops for such persons to make them understand the importance of hygiene in life. Such automated systems may also enforce the fine to such persons to demotivate them to involve in misconduct through monetary losses. The proposed system works on Resnet50 architecture to detect and recognize such activities. This pre-trained model is trained transferred in our application and is trained on the dataset that we have prepared for human activities like spitting, throwing garbage, wearing a mask, and not wearing a mask. After the activity recognition, the haar-cascade classifier detects the human face in the activity and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) algorithm with Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) recognizes the person from the database available with us of that organization.

articleTitle: A Survey of Erase Operation in NAND Flash Memory
abstract: Now a days the need of portable computing devices are growing expeditiously. For making these devices light-weight, shock-resistance, energy-efficient, and small in size, the manufacturers need a data storage that can fulfil all the above mentioned features. NAND Flash Memory become the excellent choice for data storage because it has all the required characteristics. “Erase-then-Write” operation is the major concern of the NAND Flash Memory. Before updation of any page, the block containing that page has to erase. The erase operation of Flash-block increase if system generates the frequent update operation. Flash Translation Layer and Write Buffer Cache Management have been proposed to minimize frequent write/update operation. In this paper we have reviewed the major proposed approaches.

articleTitle: Security Attacks Prediction Model for Cloud Computing
abstract: Cloud computing has become an indispensable computing platform of today's Information Communication Technology (ICT) world. The virtual environment provided by the cloud computing applications is neither under control of Cloud Service Providers (CSP) or users, completely. Consequently, it elicits the challenge of preventing security breaches considering that the data shared or stored in cloud computing environment can be crucial in nature. It is required to develop a system with capabilities to anticipate future security attacks. In this paper, we propose a security attacks prediction model which is based on Bayesian Networks, a probabilistic graphical model. The proposed Security Attacks Prediction Model (SAPM) takes vulnerable root causes of security loopholes, processes them through the Bayesian network and predicts the probability of security attacks.

articleTitle: Nature-Inspired Algorithms Analysis on various Benchmark Functions using Python and Golang
abstract: Recently, the Nature-Inspired Algorithm for problem-solving is now the field of interest for many researchers. The aim of this research work is to analyze the computational time and other properties from the aspect of using Python and Golang languages for naturally inspired computing algorithms. Nature-Inspired algorithms usually require immense computational capability and ease of implementation, hence in this paper, we will identify which freely available platform among Python and Golang is better for reliable performance and tremendous productivity of Nature-Inspired algorithms. By implementation of four Nature-Inspired algorithms on both python and Golang we will compare the computational time of each. Finally, we will show by drawing the graph that Golang is way better than Python for the computation when dealing with nature-inspired algorithms.

articleTitle: The Road-ahead for E-healthcare 4.0: A Review of Security Challenges
abstract: The security, privacy, and confidentiality problems posed by E- Healthcare data demand a re-examination of traditional information security principles and procedures. With the penetration of IT services in Healthcare domain the Healthcare in genre 1.0 has evolved as E- Healthcare genre 4.0. While in genre 1.0 the healthcare domain was greatly dependent on practitioner's handwritten notes to preserve their patients' medical history, in genre 2.0 the paper records have been started to be replaced with computerized records (EHRs). E-Healthcare 3.0 was centered on the patient allowing him to store and preserve his medical records. Since last one decade the E-Healthcare 4.0 has come with the inclusion of Fog Computing (FC), Cloud Computing (CC), Internet of Things (IoT), and Tele-Healthcare advances to disperse information among a few partners. With the rapid evolution of IT sector inside healthcare domain, the security challenges for E-Healthcare domain have also started to arise. This paper discusses such challenges and their proposed solution.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient Approach for the Security of IoT Networks using SCEER
abstract: The reliability of an IoT system is determined by the values of quality of service parameters (QoS) and the security of the users. Taking into account the increasing usage of IoT and its resource-constrained nature it is sometimes difficult to provide security to the users and also maintain the QoS of the networks. In this paper, we propose a routing algorithm, Sidechai based Energy Efficient Routing (SCEER) that provides security using sidechain and uses trust-based routing for the selection of appropriate routes. The performance of the networks has been studied in the presence of masquerading attacks, flooding, and Sybil attack in different scenarios. The algorithm has been implemented for a network that will be helpful for the patients to find the doctors and communicate with them to receive medical help.

articleTitle: Harnessing Machine Learning Algorithms in Universal Electronic Payments
abstract: Mobile payment services are considered by so many to be the next generation of payments. In the world we currently live in, many renowned tech companies already provide a payment service option to allow payments to occur from personal devices such as smart phones. The problem with many of these payment services is that they are no different from a credit card. They replicate the exact formula of what a credit card is supposed to do but from people's fancy phones, without providing any sort of useful or additional feature for the benefit of the user, making these payment services not very encouraging for people to utilize. Therefore, the aim is to develop a new mobile payment app called UPay. UPay provides users with a state-of-the-art payment gateway and helps them forecast their future spending by understanding trickle-down specifics to adjust their expenses using a user custom-made recommendation model. The solution is developed with Android Studio™ IDE using JAVA ™ as the main programming language for the app. Also, Firebase is used to carry the data and has a custom Machine Learning model to process the stored data to be able to reveal specific information on certain patterns. The result is a mobile payment app that is easy to use, secure with innovative features that help users understand their spending with forecasting analysis down to the very specifics. On the other hand, UCM a Tablet-Based application obtains data from the user-side App which allows the creation of a character model to understand the user better.

articleTitle: On the efficacy of Pedestrian Detection in Indian Road Scenario
abstract: Pedestrian detection has been a popular computer vision problem for the better part of two decades. With many available datasets in this context, the problem has seen a lot of attention with a variety of approaches developed for it over the years. However, the majority of the research in this context has been done in developed nations with structured roads and highly ordered pedestrian movement. The applicability of such context and the solutions working over it, in chaotic scenarios like that of Indian roads, is limited. The creation of such context is also usually challenging as data collection and annotation are both demanding tasks. In this work, we present the performance comparison of a widely used object detection framework, Faster RCNN, on roads of New Delhi and demonstrate the limitations of the training done using western datasets. We also give our analysis some relevant context by demonstrating the performance improvement after transfer learning on a dataset self-recorded on the busy roads of New Delhi and annotated using a novel video annotation tool LabelVDOS.

articleTitle: Abstract of Keynote talks
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the keynote presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: River Course Change Detection using Remote Sensing Imaging
abstract: This work examines the use of various segmentation techniques and remote sensing in mapping the course of the Padma River from the year 1988 to 2018 so as to identify and measure the changes that has taken place in the status between these periods. Various methods for segmentation were studied. These include working with classical filters, to using ArcGIS, to Fuzzy set-theory based methdods. Testing was done using measures such as structural similarity, entropy, PSNR values amongst others. The resultants found that segmentation based on fuzzy c means gave robust and efficient results. The testing was carried for images on the Padma River's remote sensed images for the years 1988 – 2018. The major changes were detected Char Janajat area. The images were collected from the NASA Earth Observatory image set.

articleTitle: Lightweight Review: Challenges and Benefits of Adopting DevOps
abstract: This review gives a clear picture of DevOps and its benefits when it is adopted by an organization. This study is based on the formal guidelines for the systematic literature review process. We used the standard methodology for the preparation of literature review, we employed a manual search with the use of search strings that have a DevOps as a center topic and this manual search has been done on four databases. The objective of this study is to review the current status of DevOps from 2010 to 2020 using primary and secondary studies to review the articles related to DevOps.

articleTitle: Software Centric Driver Fatigue Discernment System Using Computer Vision
abstract: In recent times, there has been a massive multiplication in the number of vehicles seen on the road. With this increase, there has, unfortunately, also been a significant rise in the daily recorded cases of road accidents. One of the topmost causes of road mishaps is tiredness of the driver driving the automobile. Distraction caused due to tiredness can be shunned by recognizing the moment when the driver is getting drowsy and alerting her/him. We aim to contribute to creating a system which determines the state of drowsiness and sends an alert to the driver so accidents can be prevented. We set up a real time face detection using a pre-trained facial landmark detector which marks different parts of the face by coordinates. Out of all the features detected, the eyes and mouth are fixated upon. We calculate the opening and shutting of eyes and the mouth as a descriptor of tiredness using different metrics. Then these metrics are measured against a threshold value for determination of fatigue. At last, if the detector labels the person as drowsy, an alarm goes off alerting the driver and deferring a mishap.

articleTitle: Intelligent Visual Interface for Assisted Digital Teaching Using Computer Vision
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has impacted the world severely. With the onset of lockdowns and restrictions, daily activities have been hindered, forcing humanity to adapt to this new reality. With new arising necessities, several advancements have been made to help bridge the gap in our old way of life and our new, albeit forced reality. Education has been revolutionized out of necessity as well. Schools and universities have shifted to online mode in order to continue educating the future generations. But this has had its limitations. The goal of our research is to enable educators to seamlessly communicate and learn like they would on through regular blackboard. We have actuated with the use of computer vision and camera to capture their ideas onto the computer screen. Our approach involves a virtual keyboard that can be interfaced with hand gesture for providing input onto the system at a desired text area. Also, a virtual drawing system is developed that can capture finger movement and accurately draw, thereby envisioning free hands teaching gestures onto the screen.

articleTitle: Design of Automated Appliances using Internet of Things
abstract: In industries and organizations, most of the energy wastage is due to human carelessness like not switching off fans or lights before going out of the respective cabins or room. Various solutions are proposed that are based on building IoT devices rather than building an intelligent IoT system. Devices like Bluetooth, proximity sensors were used as an interfacing medium to operate appliances with mobile phones or with voice rather than having appliances learn on their own. The proposed solution aims at building a smart IoT device that operates automatically and also learns from the surrounding.

articleTitle: Heart Rate and SPO2 Monitoring App while Exercising Squats for Smartphone
abstract: This paper's goal is to design and develop a mobile application for smartphones using in-build and external MAX 30100 sensors for health monitoring purposes. Application developed is capable of monitoring the heart rate and oxygen saturation (SPO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) levels while performing the squat exercise. Further, the collected data can be sent to a server so that users can check their recorded vitals from the past, and the collected data from multiple users may be used for analysis to draw meaningful medical insights. Accelerometer and gyroscope sensors are used to count the squat of a person that he/she has performed in real-time. The application also has a facility to calculate BMI.

articleTitle: Optimal Resource Allocation during Epidemics using Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Epidemics can prove to be disastrous, which has been further emphasized by the recent COVID-19 pandemic, and several countries like India lack sufficient resources to meet the population's needs. It is therefore important that the limited testing and protective resources are utilized such that the disease spread is minimized and their reach to the most vulnerable demographic is maximized. This paper studies the scope of intelligent agents in aiding authorities with such policy-making decisions. This is done by exploring the performance of various action selection methods on custom environments dealing with socio-economic groups and Indian states. Experiments using multi-armed bandit techniques provide greater insight into administrative decisions surrounding resource allocation and their future potential for greater use in similar scenarios.

articleTitle: Towards Efficient Forecasting of Web Articles using Fibonacci Median
abstract: As the number of internet users is increasing day by day, the traffic over the internet is getting q uadrupled in its volume. This work tries to forecast the traffic o ver t he internet by presenting an approach based on the log transformation and the usage of the Fibonacci median for the feature selection process. The results of the technique have been compared with the standard LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) and ARIMA (Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average) models. It has been observed from the analysis that our proposed approach provides better results compared to the LSTM technique in terms of lower RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) and SMAPE (Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error) values. However, these resulting errors are still more than that of ARIMA model. This technique can further enhance the performance of already existing methods and open prospects for a better user experience on the internet.

articleTitle: Depression Detection on Social Media
abstract: The paper presents a comprehensive approach for the detection of symptoms of depression in individuals based on their data from a social media network, Twitter. This data is combined with a historical labelled data set for gaining proper insights about users. Apart from its large size, data of user tweets is of an unstructured form and hence, the work employs a MongoDB based Big Data framework for storing and processing this data. Naïve Bayes' and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) classifiers are used to classify tweets as belonging to depressed users or not. Subsequently, topics are extracted from the tweets using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) to understand the key terms in depressed users' tweets. Lastly, a chatbot based solution is presented for helping the depressed users.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Degree of Redundancy for Replication in Distributed Database System
abstract: Allocation, and replication of fragments at sites is a challenging task. After fragmentation, allocation should be done in an efficient way, such that the transmission cost, and global access is reduced. Availability of fragment is an important issue to reduce the cost. Replication of fragments is necessary whenever another site is also frequently accessing the fragment. Finding the suitable amount of replication or degree of redundancy is required to increase the availability. This paper provides a way to ascertain the number of copies of fragment (benefit of degree of replication) that should be placed on different sites. With the increase in the degree of redundancy, there is no progressive increase in the benefit of degree of replication. If the number of replicas is between two to four, then the benefit of replication is increasing progressively. This increases the availability of data, reliability of system, reduced network load, and supports parallelism. Beyond this, increasing the number of replicas is proportionally less beneficial.

articleTitle: Effect of Hyper-Parameter Tuning on the Performance of Augmented Random Search
abstract: Recently, researchers working in the field of Artificial Intelligence have been keen on finding new algorithms that provide optimal results. One such reinforcement learning algorithm is the Augmented Random Search. This algorithm is imperative as it provides better results over other reinforcement learning algorithms. Finding the optimal values of hyper-parameters helps the algorithm to work up to its full potential. In this work, we have made an effort to find out the best hyper-parameter settings for the learning rate and direction, for this specific task. Our results show how a change in these values can impact the final maximum rewards obtained during the training process. We report novel findings of the impact of hyper-parameters on the performance of ARS algorithm. Finally, an effort has been made to find out by what percentage the ARS performs better than other Reinforcement Learning algorithm, TRPO.

Author Keywords: Augmented random search Reinforcement Learning Hyper-parameter

articleTitle: SaveLives - A Real-Time Threat Detection System
abstract: These days CCTV cameras are everywhere - malls, schools, shops, public places etc. But still people are able to commit crimes and run away because the police or the authorities are notified very late and are thus unable to do anything. Guns and knives are the most common weapons used in committing crimes today. We propose SaveLives - a system which can detect guns and knives from video footage in real time and thus notify the authorities instantly, so that they can come at the right moment and intervene. Unlike today's surveillance systems, it doesn't require human supervision. Our system also eliminates false positives by cross checking against registered faces like that of policemen or security guard. After the system detects a gun or a knife, Twilio API is triggered to alert the concerned authorities about a possible terrorist attack or a threat to public safety, so that timely action can be taken. This paper presents a system for detection of guns and knives based on Yolov4. We achieved Mean Average Precision (mAP) score of 90.35% and Average Intersection Over Union (IOU) score of 73.68%. Our proposed framework helps to stop crimes and reduce the damage done by criminals, thus saving lives.

articleTitle: Nature Inspired Algorithm towards Influence Maximization in Social Networks
abstract: Social Network allows users to interact and form relationships. These relationships build trust which influences the decisions users make. The decision could be regarding the adoption of products or behaviours. Due to the diffusion of influence in a network, a large number of organizations are benefitted. Organization's basic objective is to maximize the influence of its product or a brand. To create an impact of their products maximally organizations try to identify the seeds or influential users in a network. This paper finds out the optimal set of influential users based on ant colony optimization algorithms. The paper uses Information Cascade Model (ICM) to analyze and compare the influence spread of the influential users which has been observed from ACO algorithm by applying varied heuristics. The experimental evaluations have been done on facebook dataset, and the results show that finding influencers using betweenness centrality heuristics attain maximum influence spread.

articleTitle: A Systematic Study of Nature Inspired Algorithms
abstract: The nature-inspired algorithms are a set of algorithms widely used to solve problems that are inspired by natural objects. This paper presents the review of different nature-inspired algorithms like Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Bat Algorithm (BA), Salp Swarm Algorithm, hybrid PSO-WOA algorithm, and hybrid WOA-BA algorithm. The contribution of this paper is two-fold: we provided the details of nature-inspired algorithms and real-world applications; research gaps and comparative study of past research work have also been presented in this survey paper in order to provide a roadmap to the researchers who want to work in the same field.

articleTitle: An Empirical Investigation of a Fault Tolerant Containerized Application Deployment
abstract: Container-based deployment of applications is rapidly becoming popular since containers are lightweight, quickly deployable and allow scalability through efficient resource utilization. This paper presents a fault-tolerant architecture for a fail-safe and cost-effective containerized deployment of an application. Various modules of the application are deployed in separate containers and replicas of the critical containers are maintained for failure recovery. The multi-container architecture is compared to a multi-threaded, single container deployment. It is observed that the multi-container application outperforms the single container application in terms of cost and time of execution.

articleTitle: Analyzing Diffusion Process in Signed Networks
abstract: In today's world, our social groups are best defined by online social networks. It includes all aspects of our life including our feelings towards one another. The study of our feelings or relationships in a social network aid to form a signed network. This signed network helps us to analyze positive and negative relationships for opinion mining. In this paper, we design an information diffusion algorithm that helps in influence maximization for idea propagation in signed networks. The strength of the interaction is a key factor upon which the algorithm is designed. Epinions dataset of 131828 nodes and 841372 edges is considered for analysis and demonstration of proposed work.

articleTitle: Detection of DDOS Attack Using IDS Mechanism: A Review
abstract: There are many problems with the Internet right now, but one of them is called “Distributed Denial of Service attacks.” Various ways of protecting against this type of attack, which has become more common in the time being studied, have been thought up by people. Even so, there hasn't been a way to completely stop the attacks that have been made. It is very important for people who work with computer security to be able to spot and protect against DDoS attacks. Scientists have written this paper to look at how to find out if your computer is being hit by a DDoS attack. This is what we know about detection from reading. You need to think about things like techniques, variables, tools, deployment location, time, and detection accuracy when you do this kind of study. Each method used to find out about attacks exploits certain things about network traffic, user requests, and certain types of tools, it was found. In the end, it was able to figure out which methods are the best at detecting things, like the datasets they use, Good DDoS detection analysis can be very useful when it comes to coming up with a good strategy for stopping the attacks. People are trying to get rid of the web technologies that are needed for services to work. This has led to more people trying to get rid of them. Attacks on web servers that use the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) can happen. People try to stop them from working. DDOS is one of the most dangerous Internet attacks because it can slow down or even shut down a web server. This type of attack is called distributed denial of service, or DDoS. This paper looked at 12 recent detections of a DDoS attack at the application layer, from January 2014 to November 2021, that were made at the application layer. There is a table that sums up each detection method, as well as a critical review of each, for future research. This way, future studies can look into how to detect HTTP DDoS attacks.

articleTitle: Features Driven Brain Tumor Detection Using Machine Learning Models
abstract: Brain tumor detection seeks to separate tumorous brain images and healthy images, which is considered to be the first step in diagnosis in order to maximize the likelihood of successful tumorous region detection accuracy. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a viable input in brain tumor anatomy, which helps it in making an effective diagnosis system. To handle this research issue, a feature driven brain tumor detection model is proposed which takes BraTS 2015 MRI images dataset as input and provides segmented result label as output. The dataset contains T1, T2, T1Gd, and FLAIR modalities for each patient. The input data is preprocessed, wherein it is first converted from the .nii.gz format to NumPy arrays, and then divided into 4 subsets namely HGG-1, HGG-2, HGG-3, and LGG-1. The images are then cropped to discard the unnecessary background and to narrow the object region for all the four modalities. Feature extraction and Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) generation is then done based on the cropped image. Fourteen Haralick textual features are computed from the GLCM Matrix and standardization of the independent features using feature scaling presents data in a fixed range. Finally, supervised machine learning classification algorithms, namely Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Random Forest are used to train the model. Out of all, Random Forest algorithm reached the highest performance accuracy.

articleTitle: Wind Speed Forecasting Methods for Wind Energy Generation
abstract: To estimate the wind's uncertainty, a plethora of wind speed estimators are available, this is crucial for estimating the grid's wind energy production availability. Various approaches to estimating wind speed have been proposed. A single of major issues uncertainty is a challenge for power system operatives besides fluctuation of the wind power supply. Under the essential challenges linked through the addition of wind power into the energy grid, better predictive technologies are urgently required. This survey will also assist wind farm owners in understanding the present capabilities of wind prediction models and giving a concept for them of which techniques will be best to estimate wind speed at its wind power stations. This study will be extremely beneficial to novel scholars in this field. This study provides a chronological outline of the broad background of wind speed research and improvements for wind energy prediction.

articleTitle: Accent classification using Machine learning and Deep Learning Models
abstract: Accents are speech habits that different language speakers' exhibit. Usually, they have common traits for people of similar racial, cultural, or social context. Speech categorization is the question of finding accent type of the fellow citizens of different geographical locations. By speech classification, one can easily identify where the person belongs, his personal locations as well as religious backgrounds. But not always this speech classification thing is useful. Obviously, it is bound to make mistakes if done manually. Sometimes people refer to some accents or languages that hardly anyone uses or has ever heard of. This poses a challenge for most people as they do not understand it and fail to interpret the true meaning. Hence, this paper developed a model by utilizing machine learning and deep learning algorithms to create an effective tool for accent classification. The proposed system is validated using Speech Accent Archive dataset hosted by George Mason University on Kaggle. Results show that among various machine learning models, Decision Trees performed best even when it is compared to deep learning models such as CNN and LSTM and achieved an accuracy of 97.36%.

articleTitle: Analysis of clustering algorithms for Speaker Diarization using LSTM
abstract: Speaker Diarization is a sub-field of speaker recognition whose task is to identify the duration and number of speakers in a conversation. In a multi-speaker environment, it becomes quite difficult to segregate speaker count. In various scenarios like meetings, conferences, dinner parties, and telephonic conversation diarization helps in knowing the solution of the prolonged question “who spoke when”. Instead, it had progressed remarkably well from the last decade after integrating with neural networks. With the advent of neural embeddings, the results achieved using d-vector are better than i-vectors & x-vectors. Clustering plays an important role in identifying the speaker's label without knowing the identity. In this paper, analysis of speaker diarization pipeline which uses LSTM based embeddings of d-vectors on various clustering techniques is done. This pipeline has been implemented on the recently introduced VoxConverse diarization corpus consisting of meetings, broadcasts, and telephonic conversation recordings. Spectral Clustering performed well on this dataset and resulted in the lowest Diarization Error Rate (DER) as compared to other clustering techniques that have been taken under this study.

articleTitle: Statistical Optimization of FPN Hyperparameters for improved Pedestrian Detection
abstract: Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) has recently been extensively applied in the area of object detection for its multi-scale framework. A majority of tasks utilizing FPN use the pre-trained models or the popular architectural variations as-is. We argue that the architecture to be used depends upon the problem being tackled and that the performance is tightly correlated with the key architecture parameters. We demonstrate our hypothesis on the task of visible pedestrian detection where the bounding boxes are of varied shapes and sizes. To study the impact of various network parameters and to identify suitable values for them, we propose a statistical method based on the property of the dataset being used. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the statistical selection of the parameters on the task of Caltech-USA pedestrian detection and show that with RetinaNet, the modified network performs significantly better on miss rate and mean Average Precision than the baseline network.

articleTitle: A Study for the Development of a Photogrammetry Based AR and GR Projection System and Examining its Further Application
abstract: With the ever-growing tech industry, an incredible amount of strides are being made everyday to make our interactions with these technologies absolutely seamless. The technologies mentioned in this paper can help developing a system that will bring new possibilities in the fields of Healthcare, Education, Defense and various others. This paper will be discussing a system via the aid of Augmented Reality along with Gesture Recognition that will act as the medium of interaction between the user and the system. This paper examines existing literature on photogrammetry, augmented reality and gesture recognition respectively. An important part of the study will be investigating further implications of how the system will be embedded within other already existing stale applications. Fields like Healthcare and Defense still have some unexplored and untapped sectors that require state of the art technology. There will be some research-based analysis for different methodologies accessible to aid making these technologies more accessible to the general public.

articleTitle: FILM.LrTL: FusIng MuLtiFocus IMages using Low-rank Transform Learning
abstract: This work introduces a novel technique for fusing the multi-focus images using Low-rank Transform Learning. Multi focus images are images captured from different sources. The idea is to fuse such images to make a single image which captures all the details. For such details, capturing both local and global structures is important which is taken care of by Low rank Transform Learning. The foremost step is to segment the source image into many patches using the sliding window technique. Then HoG features are obtained to categorize these mini images. On these mini-images, Transform Learning is applied to learn sub-transforms w.r.t. each class. Then, these sub-transforms are merged into a global transform in the low rank form to obtain LRR coefficient vector corresponding to each patch. Finally, the image fusion strategy is used to obtain the final image. The convergence guarantees are established on well-sounded techniques called as the alternate minimization in proximal operations. The set of experiments show that the proposed method outperforms many classical techniques quantitatively.

articleTitle: Virtual Bazar-An Interactive Virtual Reality Store to Support Healthier Food Choices
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) has been incorporated in almost every possible application domain, but majority of the online shopping platforms are providing their customers only simple two-dimensional image-based and text-based interfaces to shop upon. This kind of monotonous shopping environment not only makes consumers lose their interest in shopping but also restricts personalized services to consumers such as providing healthier alternatives to the products or providing with suggestions based on their past shopping pattern [1]. Keeping these issues in mind the prototype of a VR based game “Virtual Bazar” is proposed which allows its users to shop in a Virtual Reality supermarket environment. The proposed model keeps a check on the Calorie requirements set by the user, shows Nutritional Information of products and create awareness for Healthier Products. It consists of two runs, in the first run users add items to their cart based on their desires with no warnings and nutritional values being shown. In the second run users are shown Nutritional information regarding products along with warnings on products having high Sugar or Carbohydrate values and with these suggestions the user again adds items to the cart. Based on the items of the two shopping lists, separate scores are calculated and analyzed. 50 different people within the age bracket of 20–35 years have played this game and ANNOVA Test has been performed on the scores obtained by these players. The results suggest that the players were benefited by the game as they learnt to choose healthier products.

articleTitle: Error rate analysis of space time coded MIMO-OFDM wireless communication system
abstract: Today's enormously growing users and applications in the wireless network are demanding high speed, high throughput, and reliable wireless links. The capacity or throughput can be improved using multiple antennas at transmitter and receiver or using spatial multiplexing as a result of the MIMO system. In the wireless environment, multipath fading is a big issue that harms signal quality and reliable communication over the wireless link. The merger of MIMO and OFDM schemes offers a better solution for mitigating error rates for reliable communication and better throughput. The ‘space-time codes (STC)’ can be used with the MIMO-OFDM system that provides transmit and receive diversity to improve the capacity as well as error rate performance. In this article, Alamouti STBC and the ‘maximal-ratio-combining (MRC)’ methods are proposed for the analysis of ‘Bit error rates (BER)’ under Rayleigh fading channel. It is shown through the results that Alamouti STBC and MRC schemes are better solutions for mitigating BER in wireless communication to improve signal quality. Simulation results shows that the MRC scheme with (1× 2) and (1 × 4) antenna configurations outperforms the Alamouti scheme with (2 × 1) antenna configuration by the SNR gain of 3 dB and 10 dB respectively at the BER value of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>.
